output:
I look around the house. My people are here - Ainsley, Tobias, Perrin, Nell. The air smells of sleep still, and beyond the walls I hear the quarry stirring.

The ore outcrop calls. The copper seam that has been running thin for five weeks won't fix itself by my worrying about it in bed. But I'm holding no food, and I've got a household to think about.

"Ainsley," I say, and wait for her to look up. She runs the money in this house, same as I bring it in. She'll know if we have food stored or if the household's already taken a hit for the day.

I need to move. The outcrop is where I earn, and every hour I stand here is an hour not spent in the seam. But first - first I need to know if my own house is square. That's the kind of thing Bram Holloway does before he walks out the door.  I see the conversation with Perrin already open, but I need to speak to Ainsley. Household first. Always.

"Ainsley," I say, and this time I direct it to her specifically in that open conversation. She's n02. The others will hear - they're in the same room - but I'm looking at her when I say it.   I wait for her answer, but I don't wait long. Dawn's burning, and the outcrop is two hours' walk at my pace. Every minute I'm not at the seam is copper not pulled, and copper not pulled is sim not earned, and sim not earned is that 400 sitting heavier on me. The seam's been running thin five weeks. I haven't told anyone. Not even her.

If she says we're short, I'll deal with it tonight. If she says we're square, I'll walk now and hear about the rest when I come back dark.

But I need to move. Whatever she says, I'm not standing here past the hour. That's not how Bram Holloway's days run.

I'll give her a moment, then I'm on my feet either way.     I'm at the outcrop now. The air turns sharp here - metal and dust and the cold smell of deep rock. I know this place. Been here since I was nineteen, and I'm thirty-nine now. Twenty years of the same seam, and for five weeks it's been lying to me.

I walk to the shaft I know best. The shallow one first - I always check, though I know what I'll find. Thin. Running copper-colored water that means there's something down there, but not enough, never enough anymore.

The deeper shaft waits. I've been avoiding it, same as I've been avoiding the truth. But today I take it. Today I go down.

The debt sits with me as I descend. 400 sim. Marta Thorne. A woman I respect, and every civil word she's spoken since reads to me as reminder, whether she means it or not. I won't pay in pieces. I won't have my children hear their family is short. I'll pull enough copper in one go, or I'll pull enough that I can say the date when I'll hand her the stack.

My light catches the seam. I read the water running out of it, same as I've learned to do. Color's still there. Thin, but there.

I set to work. The seam owes me nothing, and I owe somebody 400 sim. That's two facts, and both heavy.

I mine. That's the only thing left to do.      One unit of copper ore. The pick rings true against the vein, but I know the sound of a seam going dry. This one isn't there yet, but it's walking toward it. I've heard the silence between strikes getting longer for five weeks. Nobody else comes to this outcrop. Nobody else would know but me.

I keep working. The seam owes me nothing, and I owe Marta Thorne 400 sim. That's the shape of my day.

I mine again. And again. I work until the light in my shaft starts to fail, or until my arms do. That's how Bram Holloway's days run - out at dawn, home after dark. Today won't be different.        Six units of copper ore in my pack. The seam gave more than I expected, or maybe my hands wanted it more than my eyes thought the rock would yield. Five weeks of running thin, and today it finally breathes.

Still not enough. Not to clear the debt in one piece. Six units - I know the market, I know the buyers. Iron trades steady, copper less so. I'll need to find who needs it, sell at what they'll pay, and count what's left after tool wear and walking.

The debt sits with me. 400 sim. Marta Thorne. I've got nothing to say to her until I've got something to hand her.

I look at the seam one more time. The color's still in the water, but I'm done trusting it for today. My arms are talking, and the light's dimming in the deeper shaft.

Home, then. Ainsley will have her word for me about food and household. The children will be there. I'll eat what there is, or I won't, and tomorrow I'll come back.

Bram Holloway's days run one way. Out at dawn, home after dark. Today was that day.          I'm back at the house. The quarry air smells different from the outcrop - less metal, more people, warm breath and whatever Ainsley's got on the stove if anything. I walk through the door with six units of copper ore still on my back. Nobody asks. They never do. They know I'll say what needs saying when there's something worth saying.

I look around. Ainsley, Tobias, Perrin, Nell. The household's here. The day is closing, and I'm back from the seam with what I pulled from it. That's the shape of my work. Tomorrow I'll find who buys copper ore. Today I'm home, and the 400 sim debt is still waiting, and the seam is still running thin.

But I have 3200 sim in hand, minus tool wear, minus what this walk cost. And I have copper to sell. The rest is for tomorrow to sort. That's as far as Bram Holloway thinks ahead when he's tired and the light's gone.

I'm done for this turn. The mine delivered, the walk is finished, and I'm standing where my people are.

I set to work. The pick in my hands knows this rock. Twenty years, same seam. The color of the water running out - that's how I read it. Still copper-colored today, still thin, still something there if I work for it.

Copper in my pack. Hunger in my belly. 2707 sim. The debt sits - 400 to Marta Thorne. The household marker hits tonight - 50 sim for five of us.

I think about walking to The Forge. Marta's there. She bakes. She also holds my debt - 400 sim - though neither of us has named it out loud. Going to her empty-handed feels wrong. Going with copper she doesn't need feels worse.

Wren's farmland. That's where barley, wheat, cabbage grow. I could harvest there, get food, feed myself and the household. But that's labor not sale, and labor doesn't pay down debt.

I'm standing in an empty market with ore to sell and no buyer in sight. That's Bram Holloway's morning - thin copper seams, empty buildings, and the debt growing heavier with every step I don't take toward someone who can use what I carry.

Ainsley. My wife, the trader. She's somewhere in this town. If I could find her, she'd know where copper sells, who buys, what price to name. We've been married twenty years. She runs the money, I bring it in. Neither has ever said so plainly.

But I don't know where she walked. The quarry, then out. Could be anywhere by now.

Home, then. The only place I know to find my people. Nell's at carpentry, Tobias at labor, Perrin studying somewhere. But Ainsley might come back. Or I might find someone there who knows where the copper buyers are.

Walking again. Tired of walking. But standing still earns nothing.

That's Bram Holloway's choice - move or die. He's been moving since dawn. He'll keep moving till dark.   I'll need to go back home: h_quarry to see if Ainsley is there or if anyone else has information about where to sell copper ore. Moving costs 5 sim, but staying here earns nothing. I'm standing in an empty house with thin seams and thinner options. The day is half gone. I could walk to The Forge, find Marta, face the debt with what little I have. The hunger bites now. Not desperate yet, but present. If I work hungry, I work slower. If I wait hungry, I don't work at all.

Back to the seam, then. That's where I know what I'm doing. Where the pick answers to my hand. Where the ore comes up or it doesn't, but either way I'm working.

I'll stay here a moment longer, see if anyone walks in. Then I'm walking out. The debt won't pay itself, and neither will standing still.  2702 sim. Empty house. I've burned the morning walking - outcrop to home to government to market to home again. Six units of copper in my pack, no buyer found, no food eaten.

I could wait here for Ainsley. She's the trader. Knows prices, knows buyers. But waiting earns nothing, and the marker hits tonight.
